notes: Every source and target id is partitioned once; 18 source ids and 29 target ids all accounted for.

The italicized second *required of us* is the distributed second realization of the one written שְׁאֵלוּנוּ under rules 25 and 34, and both *us* pronouns belong to the one object suffix under rule 18; the supplied *of* reaching that suffix is the verb's under rule 44's supplied-preposition clause.

s010 תּוֹלָלֵינוּ is a noun (Ncmpc, lemma תּוֹלָל), not a participle: its unit note describes it as an anarthrous substantival participle, which is the morphology of s005 only. The correct ground is rule 46's closing paragraph, where one Hebrew nominal is recast as an English head noun and a relative clause with no Hebrew clause under it, so *they that wasted* joins the noun's unit headed on the English verb. The unit's edges, status and head are unaffected, which is why the verdict stands.

דִּבְרֵי־שִׁיר → *songs* is retained as one fused unit on the parallel of rule 30's דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים → *chronicles*; the single English word writes שִׁיר's lexeme alone, so it heads there under rules 6 and 23 rather than on the construct.

מִן takes *one of* whole, headed on *one*, under rule 19's partitive sentence and rule 15's rider that a morpheme standing in the clause takes the partitive expression before an `added` reading reaches it.
The italicized *saying* is `added`; no verb of speaking stands in the Hebrew.
